title: Asymmetric Lock Capture (Thread Starvation)
pattern: A thread releases a lock and immediately attempts to re-acquire it in a tight loop without intermediate execution delays or yields.
why_bad: The releasing thread retains the lock variable's cache line in a modified state. When it re-acquires immediately, it bypasses the scheduling latency of waiting threads (which are still waking up from OS futex blocks), starving other threads indefinitely.
detection: A lock release statement followed immediately by a lock acquisition statement within the same loop block, without intermediate yield, sleep, or non-locked work.
counterexample: The loop contains an explicit backoff, yield, or sleep statement between release and re-acquisition.
source: Richard Sites 27.5.1 (p. 347), "mystery27" Lock Capture Case Study
